# `product_order`

Area: **ordering** ([all tables](README.md))

SID ProductOrder (TMF622 productOrder): the only way to create or terminate products. Processed synchronously; a rejected order is stored with its reasons.

## Columns

| Column | Type | Null | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | `uuid` | no | `gen_random_uuid()` | Primary key, generated by the database (gen_random_uuid()). |
| `created_at` | `timestamp with time zone` | no | `now()` | When the row was inserted: the database's now(), not the injected clock. Never used for billing decisions. |
| `updated_at` | `timestamp with time zone` | no | `now()` | Last change: the database's now(), maintained by the set_updated_at trigger. |
| `billing_account_id` | `uuid` | no |  |  |
| `state` | `product_order_state_type` (enum, see [README](README.md#enums)) | no |  | TMF622 state. Used: acknowledged -> inProgress -> completed, or acknowledged -> rejected. |
| `order_date` | `timestamp with time zone` | no |  | TMF622 creationDate: the injected clock when the order was placed. |
| `requested_start_date` | `date` | yes |  | TMF622 requestedStartDate as a business date in BILLING_TZ (today when omitted): the start date of add items and the termination date of delete items. |
| `completion_date` | `timestamp with time zone` | yes |  | TMF622 completionDate (injected clock). A billing run for D sees the order's effects only if this is before 00:00 of D (BILLING_TZ). |
| `cancellation_date` | `timestamp with time zone` | yes |  | TMF622 cancellationDate: when a cancelProductOrder cancelled it; set exactly when cancelled. |
| `cancellation_reason` | `text` | yes |  | TMF622 cancellationReason, from the cancelProductOrder; optional. |
| `description` | `text` | yes |  | TMF622 description; optional. |
| `category` | `text` | yes |  | TMF622 category, e.g. residential or enterprise; optional, free text. |
| `priority` | `text` | yes |  | TMF622 priority: 0 (highest) to 4 (lowest); optional. |
| `external_id` | `jsonb` | no | `'[]'::jsonb` | TMF622 externalId[]: the order's identifiers in other systems (id, owner, type). |
| `base_type` | `text` | yes |  | TMF @baseType as the client sent it (the super-class when sub-classing). |
| `schema_location` | `text` | yes |  | TMF @schemaLocation as the client sent it (a JSON Schema URI). |
